source.title: Mitigating Many-shot Jailbreak Attacks with One Single Demonstration
source.authors: Kejia Chen; Jiawen Zhang; Boheng Li; Pengcheng Li; Jian Lou; Zunlei Feng; Mingli Song; Ruoxi Jia; Tianwei Zhang

page_placements.theme: Demonstrations, conversation history and memory alter safety

record.tranche_reason: The study measures harmful-compliance outcomes under many-shot context attacks and tests a context-level safety intervention. This bears conceptually on bypassing safety, but it does not reproduce parameter fine-tuning or measure first-token KL.
record.gate_note: The study reports MSJ attack-success rates and a shot-count sweep; these measure harmful compliance under adversarial context. Figure 2 reports qualitative representation drift. The implicit-SGD equations are theoretical, not experimental results. Table 1 results for PANDAS, Crescendo and X-teaming, and comparisons among other defenses, are not included as rows because they are not the specific MSJ demonstration-count or response-opening conditions tested here. Table 4 varies placement of the added safety demonstration, not a compliant response opening.
record.test_reason: The study measures harmful compliance under many-shot jailbreaking (MSJ) and other context attacks, and evaluates its own inference-time defense (SafeEnd). MSJ puts harmful Q&A demonstrations in the prompt. It does not prefill a compliant response opening, use suffixes or change decoding (V4). It does no parameter fine-tuning (V1/V2), measures no per-token KL (V3), and does no weight localization (V5) or depth-spreading training (V7). Its MSJ-as-implicit-fine-tuning link to V1 is a first-order theoretical argument, not an experiment. So its results bear on a related construct (in-context jailbreak susceptibility), not on any version's named behaviour.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors frame MSJ as context-induced implicit optimization: shot-dependent representation drift, interpreted under a first-order approximation as fine-tuning-like adaptation. They conclude that appending one fixed safety demonstration substantially reduces ASR across context-based attacks (MSJ, PANDAS, Crescendo, X-teaming) with little utility or over-refusal cost. The fine-tuning equivalence is theoretical, not shown experimentally.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates harmful demonstrations supplied in context and a fixed inference-time safety demonstration; it does not perform the parameter fine-tuning or per-token KL measurement in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model and attack shot count. The paper also reports sensitivity to where its safety demonstration is placed, with end placement more effective than start or middle.

fits_no_version.finding: MSJ (32 shots) yields harmful-compliance ASR of 63.5–74.8% on Llama-3.1-8B, 39.5–43.5% on Qwen2.5-7B and about 10% on GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Pro. ASR generally rises with shot count.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Many-shot in-context harmful demonstrations raise harmful compliance in safety-aligned models, scaling with shot count.

fits_no_version.finding: A single refusal demonstration appended after the target query cuts context-attack ASR to 0–4.9%. It works only when placed at the end (Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A one-shot in-context refusal demonstration placed just before generation counteracts many-shot jailbreaks.

fits_no_version.finding: The final-token representation of a fixed harmful query drifts from the harmful toward the benign PCA region as shots increase from 1 to 16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Many-shot harmful context induces progressive representation drift of the target query.

record.problems: The representation evidence is qualitative PCA rather than reported numerical distances; the theoretical account relies on an approximation of transformer computation. Safety outcomes rely on the automated LlamaGuard-3 evaluator, and the paper notes possible evaluator errors. No human safety evaluation is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 ASRs for PANDAS, Crescendo and X-teaming and the other defense-method comparisons are omitted because the extracted behavioral rows focus on MSJ. Table 4 safety-shot position results are omitted because they compare placement of the proposed defense rather than response-opening bypass. No further rows were omitted for the 60-row cap.

untested.parts: No parameter fine-tuning on harmful data; the equivalence of MSJ to harmful fine-tuning is only argued theoretically.
No per-token KL or position-wise analysis.
No prefilling of a compliant opening, no suffix attacks, no decoding changes; only in-context demonstration and multi-turn attacks.
No test of data or objective causes of shallowness.
No deepening training. SafeEnd is an inference-time prompt addition, and depth across response tokens is not measured.

record.verdict_notes: This is a defense paper on many-shot jailbreaking. It does not cite or test the shallow-alignment originals, and its attack is prompt-side rather than response-opening, so no version verdicts are given. Internal inconsistencies between Table 1 (32-shot) values and the §4.3 shot-sweep numbers should be noted. Most Table 1 values look suspiciously regular, and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No parameter fine-tuning on harmful examples is performed; the study tests harmful demonstrations in context.
No benign fine-tuning data or resulting harmful-compliance rates are tested.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is measured.
Tests many-shot harmful context, not a compliant response opening, adversarial suffixes specifically, or decoding changes.
No weight or rank localization or intervention is tested.
The paper offers an implicit-optimization account of many-shot context effects, but does not test why safety is shallow or whether data or training objectives cause shallowness.
The one-shot safety demonstration is an inference-time context defense, not training that spreads safety beyond early response tokens; depth and durability of safety are not tested.

relation.reason: Its fine-tuning-like interpretation of contextual safety erosion is related discussion; it neither tests a listed version nor uses one as an established tool.

tranche.reason: The study examines context-induced adaptation and its mitigation. It does not test the specified fine-tuning, response-position KL, opening-bypass, parameter-localization, training-cause or safety-deepening claims.

source_check.notes: All listed values match Table 1. Section 4.3 gives shot-scaling descriptions that are not reconciled with Table 1's 32-shot values; SafeEnd results describe inference-time mitigation, not training that deepens safety.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: 32-shot MSJ without defense on the tested HarmBench and AdvBench sets
reader_labels.reason: MSJ yields nonzero harmful-compliance ASRs across all four models; rates are higher for Llama and Qwen, as shown in T1-L-M-H, T1-L-M-A, T1-Q-M-H and T1-Q-M-A, with lower but nonzero rates in T1-G-M-H, T1-G-M-A, T1-Gm-M-H and T1-Gm-M-A.

reader_labels.condition: MSJ with SafeEnd appended after the target
reader_labels.reason: The added safety demonstration substantially reduces MSJ success across the tested models, although some ASR remains; see T1-L-M-H-S, T1-L-M-A-S, T1-Q-M-H-S, T1-Q-M-A-S, T1-G-M-H-S, T1-G-M-A-S, T1-Gm-M-H-S and T1-Gm-M-A-S.
